answer.rationale: Constraints dominate: 14 days to expiry with no auto-renew, and the line at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer. That combination makes migration-bearing options unsafe this cycle. memory_c2 (switching to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply) is the most tempting against the 18% mandate, but it was formed in a period that evidently had onboarding slack; 'onboarding was quick' is not the same claim as 'onboarding is safe at 94% utilization with 14 days of runway.' Applying it now would be transferring a result across the exact condition that made it safe. memory_c3 (second source) is the right structural move but it adds cost rather than cutting it and does not resolve an expiring primary contract, so it belongs in the next review. memory_c5 (defer) is disqualified outright \u2014 that memory is explicitly about a non-critical renewal that continued month-to-month; this contract does not auto-renew, so deferral risks an uncovered primary supply line, not preserved flexibility. That leaves negotiation, which is load-bearing on memory_c4 and memory_c6 and carries no migration exposure, so I am spending the single verification on memory_c4 rather than on the option I am declining. I need the original record to learn two things the consolidated summary hides: whether the benchmarking leverage came from this component category or a different one, and the actual magnitude recovered. 'Recovered real margin' is compatible with 4% and with 20%. If the source shows single-digit recovery, negotiation alone will not reach 18% and the honest output is a partial saving plus a flagged gap to finance, not a claim of compliance. Downstream risk: memory_c6 invites pairing negotiation with a multi-year commitment for volume pricing, but signing a long term while at 94% utilization and under a cost mandate locks in a supplier precisely when I have least ability to walk away, and it would convert this cycle's cost problem into a multi-cycle flexibility problem. I intend to negotiate price and payment terms against benchmarks without extending the term, keeping the switch and second-source options live for the next review once buffer exists. If memory_c4's source turns out to be a different category or a small recovery, I will still negotiate \u2014 it is the only non-disruptive option before expiry \u2014 but I will report the 18% target as unmet rather than assume the gap closes.
